title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: When you one-hot encode a categorical variable, each category becomes a separate column with binary values (0 or 1). For example, if you one-hot encode the 'sex' column, you will have two new columns: $$'sex_{male'}$$ and $$'sex_{female'}$$.

title: Intercept Term in the Model
text: Including an intercept term in a model means adding a column of ones to the design matrix. This column accounts for the baseline level of the dependent variable when all other predictors are zero.

title: Column Count in Design Matrix
text: Consider how many columns are added when you one-hot encode 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$. Remember to add one more column for the intercept term.

title: Checking Invertibility
text: For a matrix to be invertible, it must be square and have full rank. Does the design matrix $$\Phi_2$$ meet these criteria?
